input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message to my daughter, but it just won’t go through. I’m not very good with these things, so I’m hoping you can help me fix it.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002.
I just checked my phone, and I see an airplane symbol at the top. Does that mean something is wrong? I’m not sure if I can make calls or use the internet right now. What should I do?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now the airplane symbol is gone, but I see something that says "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" at the top. Is that normal? What should I do next?
I just checked, and it looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I’m not sure what that means—does that mean my SIM card isn’t in properly? What should I do?
Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now I see a little signal bar at the top, but it says "2G" and "Data Disabled." Is that better? What should I do next?
Okay, I turned on mobile data and changed the network mode to 4G/5G like you said. Now at the top, I see full signal bars, it says "5G," and "Data Enabled." Is that good? What should I do next?
I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. There’s no specific error message, but it just doesn’t send. What should I do now?
I checked the APN settings like you asked, and it looks like there’s an APN called "internet," but there’s nothing listed for "MMSC." Is that a problem? What should I do next?

I found the option to reset the APN settings, and I selected it. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit nervous—if I restart, will I lose my photos or anything important? I really don’t want to lose anything.

My phone restarted and I checked the settings—now there’s something listed for "MMSC." But I tried sending a picture message again, and it still won’t go through. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated. Is there anything else I can try?

I checked, and my Wi-Fi is already turned off, but it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is still on. Should I turn off Wi-Fi Calling now and try sending the picture message again? Also, do I need to check anything else with my messaging app?
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending the picture message again, but it still won’t go through. What should I do next? Should I check the messaging app’s permissions now?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it only has permission for "phone." It doesn’t look like it has access to storage or SMS. Should I turn those on now?
I turned on both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send a picture message. It’s still not working. Is there anything else I can try?

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message to my daughter, but it just won’t go through. I’m not very good with these things, so I’m hoping you can help me fix it.

I can help you with that! To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide either your phone number, your full name and date of birth, or your customer ID? This will help me look up your account and assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

{"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}

Thank you, John. I have your account details. To help you send picture messages (MMS), I’ll need to check a few things on your phone.

Could you please let me know if you’re able to make regular calls and use mobile data (like browsing the internet) on your phone right now? This will help me understand if the issue is just with picture messages or with your overall service.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I just checked my phone, and I see an airplane symbol at the top. Does that mean something is wrong? I’m not sure if I can make calls or use the internet right now. What should I do?

The airplane symbol means that Airplane Mode is turned on, which disables all wireless connections—including calls, internet, and picture messaging. To fix this, you’ll need to turn Airplane Mode off.

Please follow these steps:
1. Open your phone’s settings or swipe down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Look for the Airplane Mode icon (it looks like an airplane).
3. Tap the icon to turn Airplane Mode off.

Once you’ve done this, check if the airplane symbol disappears from the top of your screen. Let me know when you’ve turned it off, and we’ll continue troubleshooting if needed.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now the airplane symbol is gone, but I see something that says "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" at the top. Is that normal? What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Seeing "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" means your phone is not connected to the cellular network and mobile data is off, which will prevent you from sending picture messages.

Let’s try the following steps:
1. Make sure your SIM card is properly inserted. If you’re comfortable, you can remove the SIM card and reinsert it, or restart your phone.
2. After that, check if you see any signal bars or if "Data Disabled" changes to "Data Enabled."

If you’re not sure how to do this, let me know, and I can guide you step by step. Once you’ve checked the SIM card and/or restarted your phone, please tell me what you see at the top of your screen.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
I just checked, and it looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I’m not sure what that means—does that mean my SIM card isn’t in properly? What should I do?

If your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, it usually means the SIM card isn’t inserted correctly or isn’t making proper contact. Here’s what you should do:

1. Power off your phone.
2. Locate the SIM card tray (usually on the side or under the back cover).
3. Remove the SIM card tray and take out the SIM card.
4. Carefully reinsert the SIM card, making sure it’s properly aligned.
5. Put the tray back in and power your phone back on.

After your phone restarts, check if it now detects the SIM card and if you see signal bars at the top of your screen. Let me know what you see after doing this, and we’ll continue from there.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now I see a little signal bar at the top, but it says "2G" and "Data Disabled." Is that better? What should I do next?

That’s progress! Now your phone recognizes the SIM card and has some signal. However, "2G" is a very slow network and "Data Disabled" means mobile data is still off, which will prevent you from sending picture messages.

Let’s do the following:
1. Turn on mobile data: Swipe down from the top of your screen and look for the mobile data icon (it might look like two arrows or say "Mobile Data"). Tap it to enable mobile data.
2. If possible, change your network mode to a faster option (like 4G or 5G) for better service. This is usually found in your phone’s settings under "Network" or "Mobile Network" > "Preferred network type." Select "4G/5G preferred" if available.

After you turn on mobile data and change the network mode, let me know what you see at the top of your screen (signal bars, network type, and if data is enabled). This will help us make sure your phone is ready to send picture messages.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned on mobile data and changed the network mode to 4G/5G like you said. Now at the top, I see full signal bars, it says "5G," and "Data Enabled." Is that good? What should I do next?

That’s excellent! Your phone now has a strong signal, is connected to 5G, and mobile data is enabled. You should now be able to send picture messages (MMS).

Please try sending a picture message to your daughter again. If it still doesn’t work, let me know what happens (any error messages or issues), and I’ll help you further. If it works, you’re all set!
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. There’s no specific error message, but it just doesn’t send. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your signal and data are working, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for sending picture messages.

Please follow these steps:
1. Go to your phone’s settings.
2. Find “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
3. Look for “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
4. Check if there is an APN set, and if there is an entry for “MMSC” (this is needed for picture messages).

If you’re not sure how to check this, let me know your phone’s make and model, and I can give you step-by-step instructions. If you see that the APN or MMSC is missing or looks incorrect, let me know, and I’ll guide you on how to reset it.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked the APN settings like you asked, and it looks like there’s an APN called "internet," but there’s nothing listed for "MMSC." Is that a problem? What should I do next?

Yes, having no "MMSC" listed in your APN settings is likely the reason you can’t send picture messages. The MMSC is required for MMS (picture messaging) to work.

To fix this, you should reset your APN settings to the default values. Here’s what to do:
1. In your phone’s APN settings, look for an option to "Reset to default" or "Reset settings."
2. Select this option to restore the correct APN and MMSC settings for your carrier.

After resetting the APN settings, you must restart your phone for the changes to take effect. Please go ahead and reset your APN settings, then restart your phone. Once your phone is back on, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I found the option to reset the APN settings, and I selected it. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit nervous—if I restart, will I lose my photos or anything important? I really don’t want to lose anything.

Rest assured, restarting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or important information. Restarting simply turns your phone off and back on, which helps apply the new APN settings.

You can safely restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try sending a picture message again. If you have any trouble, let me know and I’ll help you further.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

My phone restarted and I checked the settings—now there’s something listed for "MMSC." But I tried sending a picture message again, and it still won’t go through. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated. Is there anything else I can try?

Thank you for your patience. Since your APN and MMSC settings are now correct, let’s check a few more things that can affect picture messaging:

1. Is your phone connected to Wi-Fi? Sometimes, MMS may not work properly over Wi-Fi. If Wi-Fi is on, try turning it off and send the picture message using mobile data only.
2. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled? If so, try turning off Wi-Fi Calling in your phone’s settings and then send the picture message again.
3. Does your messaging app have permission to access storage and SMS? If not, you may need to grant these permissions in your phone’s app settings.

Please check these three things:
- Turn off Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi Calling (if enabled).
- Make sure your messaging app has storage and SMS permissions.

After making these changes, try sending a picture message again. Let me know what happens or if you need help with any of these steps.
Wi-Fi is turned OFF.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser

I checked, and my Wi-Fi is already turned off, but it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is still on. Should I turn off Wi-Fi Calling now and try sending the picture message again? Also, do I need to check anything else with my messaging app?

Yes, please turn off Wi-Fi Calling and then try sending the picture message again. Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS (picture messaging).

After you turn off Wi-Fi Calling, try sending the picture message. If it still doesn’t work, we’ll check your messaging app’s permissions next.

Let me know what happens after you turn off Wi-Fi Calling and try again.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending the picture message again, but it still won’t go through. What should I do next? Should I check the messaging app’s permissions now?

Yes, the next step is to check your messaging app’s permissions. The app needs permission to access storage (for photos) and SMS (for sending messages).

Please do the following:
1. Go to your phone’s settings.
2. Find “Apps” or “Applications,” then select your messaging app.
3. Tap on “Permissions.”
4. Make sure both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled.

After enabling these permissions (if they weren’t already), try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you need help finding these settings.
App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it only has permission for "phone." It doesn’t look like it has access to storage or SMS. Should I turn those on now?

Yes, please enable both "Storage" and "SMS" permissions for your messaging app. These permissions are necessary for sending and receiving picture messages.

Once you have turned on both permissions, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you encounter any issues.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned on both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send a picture message. It’s still not working. Is there anything else I can try?

Thank you for following all the steps so far. Since you have a strong signal, mobile data enabled, correct APN/MMSC settings, Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi Calling off, and the correct app permissions, you’ve covered all the main causes for MMS issues.

At this point, since the problem persists after all troubleshooting steps, I will escalate your issue to a human technical support agent who can investigate further.
